katori.description: Standard Indian stainless steel katori (~150g standard, ~120g hostel mess)

waati.description: Marathi equivalent of katori (~150g standard, ~120g mess)

plate.description: Standard full meal plate / canteen serving (~250g)

kulhad.description: Clay kulhad cup for chai or lassi (~120ml / ~120g)

piece.description: Unit piece or count (e.g. 1 roti, 1 samosa)

glass.description: Standard glass for chaas, lassi, or juice (~200ml)

home.description: Home cooked: 1.0x baseline grease/oil, authentic spices, high bioavailable nutrients

mess.description: Hostel / Office Mess: 1.25x oil/carb multiplier, diluted dal, lower bioavailable protein

canteen_thela.description: Canteen / Tapri / Thela: 1.5x reheated oil/fat multiplier, high refined sugar/starch, low fiber

items.metabolic_notes: Flattened rice is rich in iron. Fast carbohydrate digestion; squeeze lemon for vitamin C and add extra peanuts or boiled sprouts to lower glycemic spike.
Sprouted moth beans provide excellent plant protein and fiber, but white pav and oily farsan/tari create a steep insulin spike and acidity risk.
Deep-fried spiced potato dumpling encased in maida pav. Fast starch breakdown triggers an acute postprandial glucose spike; avoid pairing with sweet chai.
Roasted semolina cooked with curry leaves and mustard seeds. Moderate GI; add carrots, beans, and roasted peanuts to slow glucose uptake.
Fermented batter of rice and urad dal. Bioavailable B-complex vitamins, virtually zero fat. Always pair with protein-rich sambar rather than sweet chutney.
High plant protein from black gram dal, but deep frying increases saturated and reheated oil load. High satiety but dense calories.
Fermented crepe; higher calorie density than idli due to tawa oil/ghee coating. Pair with dal sambar.
Mashed potato stuffing boosts carbohydrate load significantly. Accompany with coconut-chana dal chutney and sambar to blunt rapid glucose absorption.
Reference protein source with complete amino acid profile, choline, and lutein. Virtually zero glycemic spike; prime budget muscle-building meal.
Dense in casein protein and calcium. Negligible carbohydrate impact; high satiety index helps prevent between-meal canteen snacking.
Pigeon pea lentil tempered with cumin, garlic, and hing. Excellent source of lysine and folic acid. Diluted watery versions in mess reduce effective protein density.
Thicker dal preparation with onion-tomato saute. Higher lipid content due to ghee/oil saute.
Traditional mild yellow pigeon pea soup seasoned with turmeric and hing, topped with a spoon of desi ghee. Very soothing on gut mucosal lining.
Synergistic cereal-pulse combo with a complete amino acid profile. Ayurvedic comfort food; easy to digest and restores gut equilibrium.
Tapioca pearls are pure refined starch with a very high glycemic index. Sautéed with roasted peanuts and ghee; triggers sharp glucose spikes followed by reactive hypoglycemia.
100% whole wheat flatbread puffed over flame. Superior to rice and refined breads; pairs synergistically with dal and raw salads.
Gluten-free traditional sorghum flatbread with exceptional dietary fiber and resistant starch. Ideal for insulin resistance, metabolic syndrome, and satiety.
Dense mineral profile (iron, zinc, magnesium). Excellent thermogenic grain for winter, blunts post-prandial glycemic excursions.
Layered wheat bread cooked with oil/ghee. Fat content slows stomach emptying, but elevates overall calorie density.
High carb load from wheat and potato starch. Pair with cold dahi/curd to moderate glycemic peak.
Severe metabolic insult: deep-fried maida bhature soaked in oil paired with spiced chickpeas. Triggers severe glycemic surge and 4-hour insulin plateau.
Kidney bean soluble fiber binds dietary cholesterol. Basmati rice has high GI; eat rajma in 1.5:1 ratio over rice with raw onion salad to flatten glycemic response.
King of Indian budget protein! Roasted Bengal gram flour with lemon, black salt, and roasted cumin. Low GI, zero added sugar, excellent satiety and electrolytes.

items.name_en: Roasted Bengal Gram (Bhuna Chana with Skin)
items.metabolic_notes: Top student & hostel snack. Extremely high fiber and resistant starch; blunts cravings for 3-4 hours without insulin spike.
Sprouting triples vitamin C and activates phytase, improving iron and zinc bioavailability. Outstanding low-glycemic plant protein.
Lactic acid probiotic culture slows gastric emptying and reduces postprandial glucose spike by 25-30% when consumed with carb meals.
Hidden sugar hazard: 1 cutting chai has ~2-2.5 tsp refined white sugar (9g). Multiple cups cause repeated insulin spikes, gut acidity, and GERD.
High dairy protein but loaded with 25-30g added sucrose. High sugar load triggers rapid glucose elevation. Choose chaas/taak instead.
Superior Indian digestive refresher. Cumin, ginger, and rock salt soothe gastric acidity and maintain hydration with zero added sugar.
Polished rice has very low fiber and high GI (73). Always combine with double dal or sabzi to minimize insulin surge.
Maida shell deep-fried in commercial reheated oil filled with spiced potatoes. Potent combination of fast carbs and oxidized lipids.
Deep-fried refined flour crust with spiced filling. Dense in trans/saturated fats and high in sodium.
White flour pav toasted in heavy butter with potato-rich bhaji. High glycemic load and saturated fat combination.
Mint-coriander-spiced water has minimal calories; potato/ragda filling drives carbohydrates. Moderate glycemic impact.
Puffed rice (murmura) has high glycemic index, balanced somewhat by raw onion, tomato, and coriander.
Fried papdis topped with potato, sweet sonth chutney, and fried besan sev; high glycemic and sodium load.
Urad dal dumplings soaked in curd; lactic acid slows glucose breakdown, though sweet sonth chutney adds sugars.
Besan chickpea batter on onions deep fried; absorbs significant oil, especially at street tapris.
Steamed fermented chickpea flour snack; low glycemic index, watch out for sugar syrup tempering in street versions.
Top tier Indian breakfast: savory chickpea crepe loaded with ajwain, coriander, and veggies. Low GI, high plant protein.
Deep-fried whole wheat dough absorbs significant frying oil; high glycemic and lipid combination.
White chickpeas are rich in soluble fiber and resistant starch, sustaining satiety and reducing LDL cholesterol.
High soluble fiber traps cholesterol and slows carbohydrate breakdown; low glycemic profile.
High protein and calcium, but restaurant preparation uses generous butter and cream; high saturated fat.
Folate and dietary nitrates from spinach combined with dairy protein; outstanding low-carb, low-GI metabolic meal.
Easiest Indian pulse to digest with minimal flatulence. Recommended in convalescence and light diets.
Lentils and drumstick spiced with tamarind and fenugreek; rich in polyphenols and dietary fiber.
Gold standard biological value 100 protein. Zero carbohydrate, rich in choline and B12.
High lean protein stimulates GLP-1 hormone release and prevents postprandial glucose swings.
Yogurt and spice marinade roasted without added frying oil; highest protein-to-calorie density.
Eating raw kachumber 10 minutes before an Indian carb meal forms an intestinal fiber matrix that cuts post-meal glucose spikes by up to 35%.
Deep-fried khoa solids soaked in hot sucrose syrup. Acute glycemic excursion and delayed lipid clearance.
Fermented maida coils fried in ghee/oil and soaked in concentrated sugar syrup; extremely high glycemic load.
Staple mess/home subji. Cauliflower supplies sulforaphane, potato contributes starch.
Mucilage soluble fiber in okra slows carbohydrate digestion and binds bile acids, supporting glucose and lipid control.
Tempered white basmati rice with cumin seeds. High glycemic index; pair with dal tadka or curd to blunt glucose spike.

items.name_en: Standard Mess Thali (2 Roti + Rice + Dal + Sabzi)
items.metabolic_notes: Classic Indian composite meal. Notice high carb-to-protein ratio (~4.8:1). Always request extra dal or dahi and eat raw salad first.
Rich in trigonelline and dietary fiber; scientifically proven to improve peripheral insulin sensitivity.
Hung curd combined with sweet mango puree and sugar; high in dairy protein and calcium, but concentrated simple sugar requires moderation.
